newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore wants more partners in IT network.
newsitem.headline: Singapore wants more partners in IT network.

text.p: Singapore wants more information technology firms to help it build a nationwide broadband telecommunications network, officials said on Thursday.

"We expect to have by the end of the year about 100 partners. There are many types of partners -- technology and education suppliers, R&D partners," Michael Yap, National Computer Board assistant chief executive, told a news conference.

A group of 17 companies and institutions on Thursday signed a memorandum of understanding to invest Singapore $115 million (US$79.9 million) for research and development (R&D) in the Singapore ONE project.
The project has the ambitious aim of bringing interactive, broadband multimedia links to every home, school and office.
The 17 companies signing on Thursday included units of Ericsson, IBM, Philips and JVC.
Yap said 14 service and application partners were signed up for the project in January, along with 15 other local companies late last year.
Gong Wee Lik, executive director of the National Science & Technology Board, one of five government bodies supporting the project, said it wanted more partners and investment.
"We will invest in order to attract investment...the whole idea is not to limit it to X million of dollars," he said.
The government has so far committed S$154 million to build the infrastructure for Singapore ONE, and an additional S$100 million was also invested by the earlier 14 partners.
An IBM official confirmed the company had plans to set up an advanced software development centre in Singapore within the next three to four months.

It would be the first commercially-based software R&D centre in ASEAN and South Asia. The official, who declined to be identified, would not disclose the value of the investment or where it would be located.
Meanwhile, the Singapore ONE partners would conduct R&D to provide the project with technologies to enable full use of the network's high speed and multimedia capabilities.

Some of these include security applications for on-line commerce and transactions, "edutainment" that delivers education or entertainment, network access for easy connection from desktop and notebook computers and new applications.
Officials said Singapore's target to become an intelligent island, fully wired by high-capacity telecommunications, would be helped by the widespread local use of high technology.
Statistics show that one in two persons has a telephone line and one in every three households has a personal computer (PC).
The government has a five-year programme to provide PC access to every school-going child.
